rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar held that a pregnant widow's waiting period ends and remarriage becomes lawful when she delivers; an Anṣārī then relayed Umar's ruling that this applies even before her husband's burial.
rows.anchor: İbn Ömer Hazretleri “o kadın hamlini vaz‘edince helâl olmuş olur” demişti

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: An Anṣārī reported that Umar said a pregnant woman is released from her waiting period upon delivery, even while her husband is still being carried to burial.
rows.anchor: Ömer b. Hattâb dedi ki: ‘Hâmil[^35] kadın zevci defnedilmeden tabutunda iken bile doğursa helâl olur’

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reports say the shorter al-Nisa (the Divorce chapter) was revealed after al-Baqara, and cite the pregnancy waiting-period verse; variant wordings place it after the widow's four-month-and-ten-day rule.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd Hazretleri’nden rivayet eylemişlerdir ki: “Sûretü’n-Nisâi’l-Kusrâ Sûre-i Bakara’dan sonra nâzil oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound reports on revelation chronology, together with the Prophet's ruling at the Farewell Pilgrimage, establish that this pregnancy verse came later and explicitly specifies the pregnant women excluded from the general widow rule, modifying that rule by abrogation.
rows.anchor: bu haml âyetinin umûmu o vefat âyetinin umûmundan[^43] bir noktasını ta‘dîl suretiyle nesh eylemiştir

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas initially wavered between the two reports and cautiously adopted the later of the two waiting periods; the Prophet's ruling became clear after Umm Salama asked him.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri ibtidâ iki rivayet beyninde mütereddid olarak ihtiyat olmak üzere “âhirü’l-eceleyn” demiş ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For pregnant women, the waiting period after either divorce or widowhood ends at delivery.
rows.anchor: hâmil kadınların talâkta da vefatta da iddetleri vaz‘-ı haml ile tamam olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever fears God, obeys His commands, respects His rights, and seeks His protection is given ease in affairs and success in righteous works, benefiting in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: Her kim de Allah’tan korkar emirlerini tutar, hukūkuna riayet ederek vikāyesine sığınırsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prescribed rulings are God's command, revealed to Muhammad and his community, unlike prior communities.
rows.anchor: Bu zikrolunan ahkâm {أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ} Allah’ın emridir {أَنزَلَهُٓ إِلَيْكُمْ} onu size indirdi sâir ümmetlerde yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear God and preserve His rulings have their misdeeds covered, for good deeds erase bad ones, and their reward is increased and multiplied.
rows.anchor: Allah onun[^45] kabahatlerini tarafından keffâretleyip[^46] örter çünkü إِنَّ ٱلْحَسَنَٰتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated warnings to fear God, paired with promises and threats, emphasize family law and the special gravity of women's and divorce matters, including the harm of misusing divorce for trivial reasons.
rows.anchor: aile hukukunun, kadın ve talâk işlerinin ehemmiyet-i mahsûsasına ve bu babdaki dikkatsizliğin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because divorce can be necessary, people must keep their sense of duty and fear of God through love or hatred, obey God's outward and inward commands, and seek protection; enduring the resulting difficulties earns great reward.
rows.anchor: gerek aşk u mahabbet ve gerek gayz u nefret sâikleriyle Allah korkusu, vazife hisleri unutuluvermeyip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When divorce is necessary, the earlier commands to witness properly, count the waiting period, fear God, and not expel women are reiterated through the requirement to house them.
rows.anchor: وَاتَّقُوا اللهَّٰ رَبَّكُمْۚ لاَ تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِنْ بُيُوتِهِنَّ يَخْرُجْنَ buyurulduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divorced women still in their waiting period should be housed, as before the divorce, in some part of the husband's residence that he can afford.
rows.anchor: Onları, -yani o boşanıp da iddet içinde bulunan kadınları boşamadan evvel olduğu gibi- vüs‘ünüzün yettiğinden kendinizin sâkin olduğunuz yerden bir kısmında iskân ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wujd means a person's means or capacity, so a wife cannot demand accommodation beyond what her husband can afford.
rows.anchor: “Vücd” insanın vüs‘ü, gücünün yetebildiği varlığı demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These housing and maintenance commands address living husbands; a widow has no claim to housing or maintenance during her waiting period and instead receives her inheritance share.
rows.anchor: zevci vefat eden kadının iddetinde süknâ ve nafaka talebine hakkı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband must not harm or pressure women to make their circumstances constricted.
rows.anchor: Onunla beraber üzerlerinde tazyik yapmak, bezdirmek için onları zararlandırmaya da kalkışmayınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pregnant-woman clause includes pregnancies known at or before divorce and those the woman senses during her waiting period; she must report them rather than conceal them.
rows.anchor: iddet bekleyen mutallakalar bir haml sâhibi iseler ki o haml gerek talâk esnasında veya daha evvel mâlum olmuş bulunsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A woman's statement is trusted about personal matters such as menstruation ending or pregnancy, and she must not conceal what God created in her womb if she believes in God and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: Ve böyle hayzın inkıtâ‘ı ve haml gibi nefsine ait hususta kadın kavliyle tasdik olunmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pregnant divorcee must be supported until delivery; because the waiting period's purpose is to establish whether pregnancy exists, pregnancy eliminates the need to wait three menstrual cycles or settle for three months.
rows.anchor: onlar ta hamlini vaz‘edinceye kadar kendilerine infak ediniz nafakalarını veriniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that pregnancy may last at least six months, up to two years according to the Hanafis, or even four years according to the Shafiis.
rows.anchor: Talâk tarihinden itibaren haml müddeti ekalli altı ay, ekseri ise Hanefiyyeye göre iki sene ve hatta Şâfiiyyeye[^54] göre dört sene uzayabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pregnancy condition limits only the stated duration of support until delivery, not the general duty to maintain women; nonpregnant divorcees also receive maintenance during their shorter waiting period.
rows.anchor: bu şartın mefhûm-ı muhâlifi hâmil olmayan mutallakalara iddetlerinde süknâ lâzım ise de nafaka lâzım gelmezmiş gibi bir mâna ifade etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maintenance for nonpregnant divorcees follows by implication because they share the waiting-period rationale, and the commands not to expel and to house women also indicate it; maintaining the lodging entails support.
rows.anchor: ihrâcı menhî[^57], iskânı vâcib olmanın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit pregnancy condition clarifies that pregnancy is the real endpoint of the waiting and support, removes doubt about potentially long pregnancies, and signals special care for pregnant women even outside divorce.
rows.anchor: İddet bekletip infak etmekten asıl maksad, haml gayesi olduğunu anlatır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit pregnancy clause also signals special consideration for pregnant women and grounds the rule that fathers pay nursing costs when the mother nurses for them after delivery.
rows.anchor: Talâk olmasa bile hamli olanlara husûsî bir itina ile bakılmasına işaret eylemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After delivery, fathers bear primary responsibility for the child's support and must hire/pay a wet nurse; mothers have custody and the child's first right is to mother's milk.
rows.anchor: Demek ki çocuk doğunca ona baktırmak, infak etmek vazifesi esas itibariyle babalara aittir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a divorced mother exercises custody and nurses the child for the father's account, he must not take the child from her and owes her nursing and care fees; if she nurses for herself, he owes no nursing fee, though other child expenses remain due.
rows.anchor: boşanmış olan ana hıdâne hakkını isti‘mâl edip de babanın hesâbına olarak ücretle o çocuğu emzirecek olursa babanın o çocuğu ondan almayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents must consult and agree fairly on nursing fees and child support for the child's benefit, with neither father being miserly nor mother making unreasonable demands.
rows.anchor: Ve mâruf vechile, yani iki tarafın hâl ü şânına münâsib ve çocuğun menfaatine muvâfık güzel bir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If parents cannot agree because the father underpays or the mother refuses or overcharges, another woman nurses the child at the father's expense; the author rebukes both parents for causing this outcome.
rows.anchor: o vakit onu babanın hesâbına diğer bir emzikçi emzirecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the child accepts no other woman's breast, the judge compels the mother to nurse for a customary fee so the child is not lost.
rows.anchor: o vakit çocuğun telefine meydan vermemek için ana ecr-i misli ile emzirmeye hâkim tarafından cebrolunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone required to provide maintenance must spend according to their means, neither giving their entire wealth nor overburdening themselves.
rows.anchor: Se‘ası olan, yani genişliği bulunan kimse genişliğinden infak etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-off should spend from their abundance with moderation, neither extravagantly nor restrictively, following the balanced spending praised in al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: ne israf ne tazyik etmeyerek itidal dairesinde yaraşanını versin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose livelihood is restricted should give according to what God has provided, with middle-income people giving moderately and the poor little.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ona verdiğinden infak etsin orta halli olan orta halli, az olan da az versin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not require anyone to give beyond what He has granted; the wealthy and poor are each obligated according to their means, and someone able to borrow may do so in good faith with later repayment.
rows.anchor: Allah kimseye verdiğinden başka[^64] teklif etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will create ease after hardship; poor families should be patient with what they can find and retain hope, while the rich should not neglect them but support them with zakat, alms, and aid.
rows.anchor: fakirler ve fukarâ aileleri de bulabildikleri ile kanaat ve sabrederek ilerisi için Allah’tan ümidi kesmemeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disorder in family and financial matters, immorality, mismanagement, disobedience, injustice, and excess can bring the collapse of a society, civilization, or country; the sura links back to al-Taghabun and forward to al-Tahrim.
rows.anchor: bir cemiyetin, bir medeniyetin, bir memleketin inkırâzına bâdî olacak esbâbdan bulunduğu

none: Turkish rendering of the verses only; no commentary to record.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows both those who stray from His path to ruin and those rightly guided to their ultimate goal; His knowledge and lordship warrant faith, trust, obedience, and caution against opposing Him.
rows.anchor: ancak Rabbindir. Çünkü O’dur ancak seni yetiştiren, herkesten de senden de a‘lem olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who stray have abandoned the true path to eternal happiness and are truly foolish, while the guided are the truly intelligent who will reach their goal.
rows.anchor: hakikatte deliler, sapıklar onlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not heed, obey, or follow the false path proposed by deniers, but must persist in his mission despite their injustice and rebellion; the admonition also extends to all rational people.
rows.anchor: münkirleri dinleme, tanıma, sözlerini tutma, sevketmek istedikleri yanlış yola gitme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequence-marking fa introduces the first practical result of the preceding assurances and the opening counsel for carrying out God's mission.
rows.anchor: Fâ-i cezâiyenin delâletiyle yukarıki te’mînâtın ilk neticesi olan bu nehiy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generosity and forbearance are virtues only when they do not promote injustice or compromise; true generosity lies in purity, sincerity, courage, and patiently teaching their outcomes.
rows.anchor: hilim, kerem ve semâhat, haksızlığı tervicde, ciddiyetsizlikte, müdahenede değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers called the Prophet deluded or misguided out of malice and wished him to flatter them by leaving their idols and injustices unchallenged; had he accommodated them, they would have flattered and affirmed his falsehoods.
rows.anchor: Zira {وَدُّوا۟ لَوْ تُدْهِنُ} arzu ettiler ki sen müdahene etsen, onları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first foundation of noble character is to refuse obedience to the deniers and avoid flattering their aims; compromising tongues and pens are far from moral greatness and reason.
rows.anchor: İşte büyük ahlâkın ilk umdesi budur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hallaf is someone accustomed to swearing repeatedly, whether truthfully or falsely.
rows.anchor: çok half, çok yemin edici çok yemin etmeye alışmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath should be reserved for necessity to establish truth; habitual oaths trivialize it, invalidate the swearer's credibility, and show disrespect toward God's name.
rows.anchor: Çok çok yemin edip durmak ise onu istihfaf[^7]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The swearer should resort to God's testimony as a last resort, only after careful thought and confidence in the truth; careless swearing reflects failure to recognize the oath's sanctity and its role in legal trust.
rows.anchor: yemin eden kimse son bir ıztırar hâlinde, onun şehadet ve kefaletine müracaat ederken bütün hakkından emin olacak vechile düşüne düşüne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent oath-taking is a worse contradiction than having no oaths, and the author cites the verse saying they have no oaths to illustrate the point.
rows.anchor: Bu ise yeminin hükmünü tanımamak demek olan yeminsizlikten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated oaths paradoxically invoke the supreme power while declaring it weak; they are a root of evil in belief and conduct, and habitual careless swearers may become accustomed to perjury.
rows.anchor: Kuvvet almak için müracaat ettiği en büyük kudretin zaafını ilan eyleyerek kendini yıkmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maheen is base and weak in judgment, self-abasing, false, worthless, and pliable toward every bad course.
rows.anchor: Alçak re’y ve tedbîri hakir, süflî düşünür, kendi kendini küçük düşürür, yalancı, değersiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hammaz is a fault-finder and slanderer who censures, backbites, insults, and goads people.
rows.anchor: gammaz şunu bunu ayıblar, ta‘neder, gıybet eder, zemm ü kadh ile bizler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who goes about carrying tales lives as a spy and gossip.
rows.anchor: koğuculukla gezer hafiyelik[^11], boşboğazlık ile yaşar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A manna lil-khayr is miserly and useless for good, and also obstructs others from doing good.
rows.anchor: Hayır engeli, hiç hayra yaramaz, gayet bahil olduğu gibi başkalarının yapacağı hayra da mâni‘olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mu'tad exceeds limits, refuses to accept what is due, and acts unjustly; an athim is laden with sin and unafraid of its burden.
rows.anchor: mütecaviz haddini aşkın, hakkına râzı olmaz, zulümkâr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An utull is a coarse, rude tyrant and glutton who grabs what he finds, speaks obscenely, and behaves cruelly and despotically.
rows.anchor: zobu kaba, saygısız, zorba, obur, bulduğunu çarpar yer, fâhiş söyler, gaddar, müstebid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zenim derives from zeneme, a fleshy hanging appendage by a goat's or sheep's ear; figuratively it resembles calling someone a sycophant or ear-marked outcast.
rows.anchor: “Zenîm” “zeneme”den müştaktır. “Zeneme” keçinin, koyunun boynunda, kulağı dibinde derisinden küpe gibi yumrucuklara

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes, including Ibn Abbas and others, explain zenim variously as an adopted or illegitimate person, a bastard, notorious evildoer, marked unbeliever, oppressor, vile person, or profligate.
rows.anchor: müfessirler[^13] İbn Abbas ve gayrılarından bunun târifinde şunları nakl eylemişlerdir: da‘î, nesebi mülhak, piç

rows.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report in Bukhari's tafsir describes a Qurayshi man with a goat-like hanging mark at his neck; Ibn Jarir and Ibn Marduye also transmit this sense.
rows.anchor: Buharî’de bu sûrenin tefsîrinde Mücâhid’den, İbn Abbas’tan şöyle rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Alusi notes and remains uncertain about the difficulty that a congenital, unchosen mark should not be counted among the most blameworthy traits.
rows.anchor: mezmum olan ahlâk meyânında sayılmaması lâzım geldiği hâlde nasıl olur da en mezmum, en aşağısı sayılır? diye bir sual vârid olduğundan Âlûsî bunun istişkâl olunduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: الآلوسي
rows.claim: Alusi says the term can describe an acquired/artificial mark, so an acquired or figurative interpretation is more suitable and accounts for the other glosses.
rows.anchor: “zeneme” söylediğimiz vechile hulkī ve sun‘î olabileceği cihetle bunu sun‘î olarak anlamak veya mecâza hamletmek daha muvâfık olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the same moral problem applies to adopted lineage, zenim should be understood in terms of acquired conduct; “sycophant” or “earringed effeminate” fits best.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı “zenîm” dalkavuk, yahut küpeli muhannes mânasına olmak muvâfık görünür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns against vile character and obeying its exemplars; its ordered, ornate accumulation of faults preserves the Quran's decorum while marking such people as beneath all who follow them.
rows.anchor: Kur’an o fenalık timsallerine itaat etmemeyi[^19] emrederken, nazmın nezâhet ve nezâketine bir şāibe kondurmamak üzere

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the descriptions do not identify one particular person: beginning with “every” makes them a general warning about each trait and their combination, past and future.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân’ın dediği gibi âyetten zâhir olan budur ki: Bu evsâf muayyen bir şahıs için değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the singular command first addresses an individual, its warning reaches any individual or collective society embodying these traits, since a community's conscience appears through its members.
rows.anchor: itaatten tahzir olunan evsâf, hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla ferde ait olmak şart değil, ferdlerden mürekkeb olan külle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not obey such people merely because they have wealth and sons, in hopes of benefiting from their resources or avoiding their power; a sane person has no other reason to yield to them.
rows.anchor: Mal sâhibi olmuş ve oğulları var diye yani servet kazanmış ve kuvveti var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking private benefit by accommodating such people are themselves base; they block good and make no gift without controlling others, while those who indulge them to avoid harm surrender to worse harm.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki onlar hayır ehli değil, hayır engelidirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noble character endures abuse, hardship, and poverty instead of obeying or flattering vile people, and faces their obstacles to open the way to good.
rows.anchor: Büyük ahlâk ise birçok ezâlara, cefâlara, yoksulluklara katlanır, sabr u tahammül eder de onlara itaat ve müdahene etmeye tenezzül etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says that whoever honors a rich person solely for his wealth loses two thirds of his religion, expressing the verse's implication.
rows.anchor: “Her kim bir zengine mücerred malından dolayı tâzim ederse dininin üçte ikisi gider”[^27] meâlindeki bir hadîs-i şerîf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “because he has wealth and sons” may attach backward to the prohibition against obedience, explain the motive for the whole list of faults, or attach forward to the next statement as the cause of one man's arrogance.
rows.anchor: Bunun rabtında da birkaç vecih vardır. Birisi mâkabline merbut olup beyan ettiğimiz vechile yukarıdaki فَلَا تُطِعِ emrine müte‘allik olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the forward-attached reading, one of them became arrogant because of wealth and sons and called the revealed verses legends of the ancients.
rows.anchor: Onlardan birisi mal ve oğullar sâhibi olduğu için mağrurlandı, burnunu şişirdi de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rendering the threat as branding him on his snout hints at pride; the snout's association with elephants and pigs and the ugliness of branding make it especially humiliating.
rows.anchor: Sonra hortum fil[^30] ve hınzır burunlarında kullanıldığı ve yüze, buruna damga

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade branding animals on their faces and cursed the person who does it.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah hayvânâtın bile yüzlerinden damgalanmasını nehiy buyurmuştur ve yapana lânet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nose is the most visible, forward part of the face and a sign of dignity and honor; it is the place of prostration and was called the seat of beauty.
rows.anchor: Yüzde burun ise en önde olduğu için en göze batan, ilk sakınılması lâzım gelen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poet says a youth's beauty lies in the nose, even when it is unadorned; a mole would make it like jewelry.
rows.anchor: وَحُسْنُ الْفَتَى فِي الأَْنْفِ وَالْأَْنْفُ عَاطِلٌ فَكَيْفَ إِذَا مَا الْخَالُ كَانَ لَهُ حُلِيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Branding the snout is a figure for extreme humiliation, material or spiritual and worldly or otherworldly; the discussion first turns to its worldly aspect.
rows.anchor: hortumunu dağlamak, damgalamak “burnunu kırmak” tâbirimizde olduğu gibi son derece tezlilden kinayedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested the deniers who trusted in wealth and sons, making those supposed blessings a trial because they used them to block good and show pride rather than give thanks.
rows.anchor: Muhakkak ki Biz onlara bir belâ verdik yani mal ve oğullarına güvenip de öyle diyenleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first proclamation, Meccans followed such immoral leaders in denying God's signs and tormenting the Prophet, so he prayed for Mudar to face severe hardship like Joseph's years; God then afflicted them with seven years of famine.
rows.anchor: “Allahım! Mudar’a darbeni şiddetlendir ve onlara Yûsuf’un seneleri gibi kıtlık ver”[^32]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard story shows that this divine law is not a chance event limited to the deniers of Muhammad's time but applies across generations.
rows.anchor: sade onlara münhasır bir tesadüften ibaret olmayıp evvel ve âhir tatbik edilmesi iktizâ eden bir kanun olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-janna means an earthly paradise, a beautiful orchard, or at a deeper level a homeland; the story was familiar to Arabs, and its owners were those who possessed and managed the orchard.
rows.anchor: burada “cennet”ten murad dünya cenneti, güzel bağ ve bostan demektir. Daha derin bakışla da vatan demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them the plural owners, unlike the single owner's garden in al-Kahf, points to common property and a social or national parable rather than an individually managed estate.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’te وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ [18/35] âyetinde olduğu gibi bir ferd misâliyle getirilmeyip أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ diye cemi‘sîgasıyla müşterek bir milk misâli olarak getirilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known account places the orchard near San'a in Yemen, at Sawran: a righteous owner gave God's due from its produce, but after his death his children withheld its benefit from people and begrudged God's due, bringing the narrated outcome.
rows.anchor: Yemen’de San‘â’ya yakın, Savran denilen arzda sâlih bir adamın güzel bir bağı vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning the social parable with the owners' oath points to how communal enterprises begin with an agreement whose guarantee is the oath and whose consequences govern profit and loss.
rows.anchor: her ictimâ‘î bir işin bir akid ve mukavele ile başladığını ve bunun yegâne müeyyidesi de yemin olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath echoes the earlier “frequent swearer” and warns that people who make firm vows without considering their knowledge or power may swear falsely and bring disaster on themselves.
rows.anchor: yukarıda كُلَّ حَلَّافٍۢ en başında zikredilmiş olduğu gibi burada da ondan başlanmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarm means to cut or harvest a vine and its fruit, or sever something completely; although they meant to gather the fruit, their oath said they would certainly cut the garden itself in the morning.
rows.anchor: “Sarm” bağ kesmek, üzüm ve meyve devşirmek mânasına geldiği gibi, bir şeyi kökünden kesip tamamen ayırmak mânasına da gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners could not control the garden's fate or even know with certainty that they themselves would live until morning.
rows.anchor: gerek o bağın gerek kendilerinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They made no exception such as “if God wills,” if they reached morning safely, or if no accident befell them, because their overconfident resolve did not consider failing their vow or a reversal of fortune.
rows.anchor: “inşaallah, Allah izin verirse” yahut “sağ sâlim sabaha çıkarsak, bir kazâ ve âfete uğramazsak” gibi bir şart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their failure to make an exception means they wanted to give nothing to anyone else and did not consider that anyone besides them might harvest the garden.
rows.anchor: Yahut kendilerinden başka kimseye bir şey vermek istemiyorlar, onu kendilerinden başka birisinin kesebileceğini hesâba almıyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While they slept, a divine command or disaster from their Lord passed around the garden on every side.
rows.anchor: Rabbin tarafından bir tâif, dolaşan bir emr-i ilâhî, bir âfet o bağın üzerinden her tarafını dolaşıverdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says a fire emerged from the valley where the garden stood and burned it to its roots.
rows.anchor: Bir rivayete göre bağın bulunduğu vâdiden bir ateş çıkıp o bağı kökünden yakıp kavurup bitirivermişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By morning, the paradise-like orchard had become a sırım, a ruined and scorched husk.
rows.anchor: Derhâl o cennet gibi bağ sabaha kadar sırıma dönüvermişti
